description: Estudiantes de biotecnología con una misión en común., innovar en el estudio de ciencias de la salud y sus aplicaciones
summary: ASTRA BioSense is a Lab-on-a-Chip and app that helps monitor astronaut health during long missions. The chip is a disposable cartridge that measures five biomarkers from saliva and urine, with no needles or centrifuge: 3-methylhistidine (muscle loss), cortisol (stress), melatonin (sleep and circadian rhythm), 8-OHdG (oxidative damage) and creatinine (to correct urine dilution). The ASTRA app compares each result with the astronaut’s own baseline, shows trends next to vital signs and raises early alerts. It addresses the challenge of monitoring health in space because most analysis today happens after the flight, so a bad trend can go unnoticed during the mission. Our demo is a conceptual prototype that uses simulated data.
details:
We built two parts. The first is a chip design: a disposable cartridge with separate saliva and urine inlets, where capillary flow moves the sample to five chambers. Four use freeze-dried antibodies for competitive immunoassays (3-MH, cortisol, melatonin and 8-OHdG), and one uses a colorimetric reaction for creatinine. An LED and a photodetector read the optical signal, and stored calibration curves turn it into concentrations. The second is the ASTRA app, written in HTML and JavaScript, which normalizes 3-MH and 8-OHdG by creatinine, plots circadian curves, classifies changes against each astronaut’s baseline as normal, watch or review, and computes a Wear and Recovery Index. It also shows vital signs from wearables.

We chose saliva and urine because drawing and centrifuging blood is impractical in microgravity. The panel connects muscle loss, stress, sleep and oxidative damage, which are risks documented by NASA’s Human Research Program. Evidence for some markers during flight is mixed, which is why we want to measure them during the mission. The app uses simulated data for six crew profiles, and the chip is a design that still needs assay optimization, stability tests and validation.
